Notes

A neat official word covers a frightening sequence: punishment, rehearsed smiles, trembling passengers and a driver who cannot see.

统称

统称 is the act of grouping different things under one name. Repetition makes 纪律 sound like a label stamped onto whatever happens next. The verse then supplies its contents: beatings, scolding, stiff movements and false smiles. The accusation sits in the gap between the tidy name and the experience it is asked to make acceptable.

  • Ministry of Education dictionary: 統稱
  • Chinese lyric transcript
谈心

谈心 suggests private, sincere conversation about someone’s concerns. The opening withholds precisely that kind of attention, then accuses the ignored person of seeking notice. Before rules become physical punishment, the song shows an emotional hierarchy: the person can be managed or dismissed, but does not get to explain what is happening inside.

  • Lyric transcript
吸引点注意

点 makes the request small: a bit of attention. Set after three statements that nobody cares or even mentions this person, the charge of attention-seeking turns neglect into the neglected person’s fault. That circular logic gives the verse’s “discipline” an intimate cruelty before it expands into crowds and systems.

  • Lyric transcript
魔术师

Miracles are scarce, and then the magician goes home: the wording moves from something supernatural to somebody who performs illusions. What remains receives the name “discipline.” Read together, the lines let that tidy label replace any promise of transformation or rescue.

  • Lyric text
一堆散沙

Loose sand is an established idiom for people who cannot hold together as a group. Each grain remains separate. Placing it after 体系, 'system,' sets up the verse's tension: organization promises cohesion, while the next lines show the punishment used to enforce it.

  • Ministry of Education dictionary: 一片散沙
  • Chinese lyric transcript
挨打完后挨骂

挨 marks being on the receiving end: first blows, then verbal abuse. The repeated structure makes punishment a sequence with another stage waiting after the first is over. It also undoes any comforting distinction between correcting behavior and humiliating a person; the system delivers both in the same grammatical rhythm.

  • Lyric transcript
手掌底下

A dense crowd is reduced to something that fits beneath a palm. The scale makes domination almost tactile, and the stiff movements that follow make the people resemble controlled figures. No controller needs to be named for the arrangement to be clear: many bodies move inside the reach of one hand.

  • Lyric transcript
笑的都很假

After the stiff movements, even an expression of happiness looks rehearsed. Discipline has reached the face: the group does not only have to move correctly, but to appear content while doing it. The later reassurance “don’t be afraid” inherits this suspicion, since the words of comfort may be another required performance.

  • Lyric transcript
油还加不加

加油 means adding fuel and is also the everyday cheer 'keep going!' or 'come on!' Here the question separates 油, 'fuel,' from 加, 'add.' The coming car scene makes refueling literal, while the encouragement meaning creates an uneasy echo beside the trembling legs.

  • Ministry of Education dictionary: 加油
  • Chinese lyric transcript
腿一直哆嗦

The mouth keeps talking while the legs keep shaking. Those simultaneous bodily actions separate the confident public statement from the fear that cannot be controlled. The doubled 一直, “all the time,” gives both equal duration: the speech does not stop the tremor, and the tremor does not interrupt the speech.

  • Lyric transcript
瞎子在开车

This is an arrangement of power in miniature. Someone unable to see still occupies the driver’s seat; the “we” has a seat but no steering wheel. Following the crowded group under one hand, the car brings collective danger into an ordinary enclosed space where the passengers must entrust movement to somebody else.

  • Lyric transcript
说走就走的旅行

说走就走的旅行 became a familiar phrase for the freedom to drop everything and travel; a 2015 China Tourism Academy speech discussed it as a youth buzzword. Here the passengers sit behind a driver who cannot see. The cheerful slogan lands inside a scene where they have little control over where they are going.

  • China Tourism Academy: Dai Bin on the phrase at COTTM2015
  • Chinese lyric transcript
千万别回头

千万 intensifies the instruction into an urgent warning. Repeating “don’t be afraid” has not made the ride safe; the final command instead limits what the passengers may look at. The travel slogan returns after this warning, now sounding less like freedom than being carried along despite fear.

  • Lyric transcript

About Jackzebra and this mixtape

Zhuang Zhuang Mixtape arrived on Surf Gang on October 2, 2026: 55 tracks, opening with Sour and closing with Sweet. Its cast widens from YoungQueenz on Poker Face to User116, Effie, kuru, yoyi, 春 and 南部犯罪份子. Aghast has a production credit on every track from Hitman through Snatch, giving that stretch a shared collaborator behind its changing scenes.

Surf Gang release · Artist credits

Jackzebra told AVYSS that he writes while singing over a beat he has listened to repeatedly, keeping the images in his head central. He values the room Mandarin leaves for indirect meanings. Listen for ordinary phrases becoming physical scenes: familiarity becomes cooking, authority becomes family seniority, and a tired saying suddenly turns into a threat.

AVYSS interview, 2024

In STATIC, he describes mixtapes as a format for letting ideas flow, reserving an official debut album for later. In a separate conversation about Above & Beyond, he compared that earlier tape to a collection of his producer friends’ work. The credits here likewise reward attention: long-running collaborators sit alongside guests working in Mandarin, Korean and English.

STATIC interview · Sabukaru interview, 2025

The small details connect to his stated interests: he has described playing Temple Run in transit and before shows, watching Top Boy, and wanting to score White Oleander. These give the songs specific points of contact with his life. The notes follow those connections alongside the lyrics’ jokes, invented scenes and competing voices.

His recommendations in Perfectly Imperfect · Dazed interview, 2025 · Interview questionnaire, 2025

Jackzebra has pushed back on being made to represent all of China’s underground. These notes stay close to the words: what an expression usually means, what changes in this line, and how another song answers it. Cultural references have sources; interpretations rest on details you can hear or read in the song.
